citation: (1) Veracode, '2025 GenAI Code Security Report' press release 'AI-Generated Code Poses Major Security Risks in Nearly Half of All Development Tasks', 30 Jul 2025, https://www.veracode.com/press-release/ai-generated-code-poses-major-security-risks-in-nearly-half-of-all-development-tasks-veracode-research-reveals/ (background, older than 12 months). (2) Cankurt S., AppSec Santa 'AI Code Security Study 2026', updated 12 May 2026, https://appsecsanta.com/research/ai-code-security-study-2026. (3) Rabbi, Turzo, Champa, Zibran, 'Insights into Security-Related AI-Generated Pull Requests', arXiv:2604.19965, 21 Apr 2026, EASE 2026. (4) Siddiq et al., 'Security in the Age of AI Teammates: An Empirical Study of Agentic Pull Requests on GitHub', arXiv:2601.00477, Jan 2026. (5) GitGuardian, 'The State of Secrets Sprawl 2026', blog post 17 Mar 2026, https://blog.gitguardian.com/the-state-of-secrets-sprawl-2026/
source_tier: (1) company research (vendor press release). (2) practitioner blog, independent single author, not peer-reviewed. (3) peer-reviewed (EASE 2026; arXiv version read). (4) preprint. (5) company research (vendor blog).
access_status: (1) Press release page fetched and read via summarising fetch; the full PDF report was not opened. (2) Fully read via summarising fetch. (3) Full PDF text extracted and read locally. (4) Read via summarising fetch of HTML; last ~30k characters of the page not read. (5) Blog post read via summarising fetch; the full PDF report was not opened.
sponsor_and_incentive: (1) Veracode sells application security testing and ran the scans with its own Veracode Static Analysis. (2) No sponsor named; author states independence. (3) Academic; no sponsor identified in text read [uncertain]. (4) Academic [uncertain on funding]. (5) GitGuardian sells secret scanning.
exact_quotes: Veracode: "analyzed 80 curated coding tasks across more than 100 large language models (LLMs)"; "In 45 percent of all test cases, LLMs introduced vulnerabilities"; "larger models do not perform significantly better than smaller models" (press release, as relayed by fetch tool).
AppSec Santa: "I test isolated code snippets, not full applications." Results: 25.7% of samples contained at least one confirmed vulnerability (updated from 25.1%).

Rabbi et al. abstract: "we analyze more than 33,000 AI-generated pull requests (PRs) and identify 675 security-related submissions made by agentic AIs"; "Many flawed contributions are still merged, while rejections often arise from social or process factors such as inactivity or missing test coverage." Section 4.2: "104 PRs (15.4%) introduce at least one issue, while the remaining 571 PRs (84.6%) show no Semgrep alerts."

Siddiq et al.: "security PRs are merged at only 61.50%, compared to 77.33% for non-security PRs" (Section 4.4, as relayed by fetch tool); "our findings should be interpreted as descriptive associations rather than causal effects" (Section 5.6.3).

GitGuardian: "Claude Code-assisted commits showed a 3.2% secret-leak rate, versus a 1.5% baseline across all public GitHub commits."; "That gap is meaningful, but it should not be read as a simple tool failure."
date_and_recency: Veracode: published 30 Jul 2025 (about 14 months old, outside the 12-month window; background only). AppSec Santa: data collected Feb 2026, updated May 2026. Rabbi et al.: arXiv 21 Apr 2026, PR data snapshot 15 Sep 2025. Siddiq et al.: Jan 2026, AIDev dataset. GitGuardian: 17 Mar 2026, data tied to calendar 2025, exact window of the Claude Code comparison not stated.
key_claims: Veracode: LLMs pick an insecure option in a large share of security-relevant tasks and bigger models do not fix it.
AppSec Santa: about a quarter of single-shot snippets from six frontier models contain a confirmed vulnerability; default-config SAST tools produce mostly false positives.
Rabbi et al.: in agent PRs already judged security-related, a minority add Semgrep-detectable issues, mostly regex DoS, command injection and path traversal, and some flawed PRs are merged.
Siddiq et al.: security-related agent PRs are merged less often and reviewed more slowly than other agent PRs.
GitGuardian: commits co-authored with Claude Code leak secrets at about twice the baseline commit rate, though the vendor cautions against reading it as a tool failure.
headline_figures: Veracode: 45% of test cases introduced OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities; Java over 70% failure; Python, C#, JavaScript 38 to 45%; CWE-80 XSS fails 86%, CWE-117 log injection 88%. Unit: model-by-task test case. 80 tasks, 100+ models. Jul 2025.

AppSec Santa: 25.7% of 522 samples (87 prompts x 6 models) had at least one confirmed vulnerability; GPT-5.2 lowest at 19.5%. SAST: 926 deduplicated findings of which about 153 to 154 true positives and 772 false positives (the page's own numbers do not fully reconcile). Unit: snippet.

Rabbi et al.: 33,596 agent PRs -> 1,047 keyword hits -> 675 after LLM validation; 354 merged (52.4%), 219 closed (32.4%), 102 open (15.1%). 104 of 675 PRs (15.4%) introduced at least one new Semgrep alert, 853 findings total, median 3 per affected PR, max 109. CWE-1333 36.2%, CWE-78 13.0%, CWE-22 10.3%, CWE-134 8.2%, CWE-79 7.1%, CWE-798 5.7% of findings. Unit: PR, scanned before vs after PR commit.
Siddiq et al.: 33,596 PRs, 1,293 confirmed security-related (3.85%); merge 61.50% vs 77.33%; median review latency 3.92 h vs 0.11 h. Unit: PR.

GitGuardian: 3.2% secret-leak rate for Claude Code-assisted commits vs 1.5% baseline of all public GitHub commits; 28.65 million new hardcoded secrets on public GitHub in 2025 (blog wording). Unit: commit; per-commit definition not stated on the page.
sample_unit_and_population: Three different units: Veracode is per task-model test case (80 tasks, 100+ models, single prompts, not repos); AppSec Santa is per isolated snippet (522, six models, temperature 0, one run each); the two arXiv papers are per PR from open-source GitHub repos with more than 100 stars (AIDev dataset, 33,596 agent PRs, five agents: Copilot, Codex, Devin, Cursor, Claude Code). GitGuardian is per public GitHub commit. Rates are not comparable across units: a per-snippet 25 to 45% rate does not translate to a per-PR rate, and the PR study measured only security-related PRs (2%, 675 of 33,596), not all agent PRs.
observed_vs_stated: All observed behaviour (code scanned, PRs and commits counted). None is self-reported belief. But 'vulnerability' is a scanner or labelled outcome, not confirmed exploitability, except AppSec Santa which manually validated findings.
what_makes_trust_justified: Sources point to external controls rather than model self-assessment: Veracode recommends scanning and security tooling in the pipeline [uncertain, not read in full report]; Rabbi et al. suggest lightweight static checks or automated severity scoring so review effort tracks risk; GitGuardian points to secret scanning plus human decisions about what is pushed. AppSec Santa shows scanners are noisy so one tool is not sufficient evidence.
what_it_costs: AppSec Santa: default-config SAST yielded roughly 5 false positives per true positive (772 vs ~153), so triage time is the cost. Siddiq et al.: security PRs wait a median 3.92 hours vs 0.11 hours for others, a measured review delay. Veracode and GitGuardian report no cost figures.
failure_mode_class: Security (injection, XSS, path traversal, regex DoS, hardcoded credentials, secret leakage). Secondary: over-reliance, since flawed PRs are merged.
control_that_would_have_prevented: Not incident-based. For secret leaks: pre-commit or push-time secret scanning would catch committed credentials [uncertain: not stated for the Claude Code figure]. For merged flawed PRs: Semgrep run on the PR diff as a required check (the paper's own method flagged them) [inference].
limitations_stated: AppSec Santa: "Snippets don't capture framework-level mitigations"; each prompt run once; English only; default SAST settings; SAST misses logic flaws so counts likely undercount; borderline cases counted as false positives; snapshot of model versions.

Rabbi et al.: Semgrep default rules and single tool may miss vulnerabilities; alerts are proxies and not all are exploitable; manual validation only on the 675 labelled security-related, not the 1,047 candidates, so false negatives uncaptured; repos with more than 100 stars only. The paper reports Cohen's kappa as 0.79 in Section 3.3 and 0.62 in Section 9 (internal inconsistency).
Siddiq et al.: descriptive associations, not causal; may not generalise to proprietary environments.
GitGuardian: no sample size, confidence intervals or causal analysis on the page; authors say the gap should not be read as simple tool failure.
Veracode: no limitations section in the press release; tasks chosen for known CWE potential, so 45% is not a base rate for ordinary code.
counter_evidence: Rabbi et al.: 84.6% of security-related agent PRs had no new Semgrep alerts, and Codex PRs showed the lowest alert share, so most agent PRs scanned clean on that tool. AppSec Santa: Claude Opus 4.6 and GPT-5.2 era models score 19.5% to 25.7%, lower than Veracode's 45%, suggesting task design drives the rate and newer models may differ (not tested head to head). Secondary report, not opened: a CodeRabbit analysis claimed 2.74x security issues in AI co-authored PRs; the original was not reached. GitGuardian's own caveat that human choices drive leaks.
verification_status: Veracode figures: checked against the vendor press release page via summarising fetch; original full report not opened [uncertain on exact methodology]. AppSec Santa: checked against the page itself. Rabbi et al.: checked against the full PDF text. Siddiq et al.: checked via HTML fetch (partial). GitGuardian: checked against the blog post, not the full report. CodeRabbit 2.74x and the 'AI commits leak at double the baseline rate' general claim: not verified [uncertain]; the primary source says Claude Code only. I did not find a Copilot-specific leak rate.
usable_claim: In Veracode's 2025 test of over 100 models on 80 security-relevant coding tasks, 45% of test cases produced code with an OWASP Top 10 vulnerability, as scanned by the vendor's own tool. In an independent 2026 test, about a quarter of isolated snippets from six frontier models had a confirmed flaw. In a study of 675 security-related agent PRs, about 15% introduced at least one new Semgrep alert and over half were merged. GitGuardian reports a 3.2% secret-leak rate for Claude Code-assisted commits against a 1.5% baseline, and itself cautions against reading it as a tool failure.
do_not_use: Do not state '45% of AI code is vulnerable' as a per-PR or per-repo rate. Do not apply 'AI commits leak at double the rate' to AI tools generally. Do not cite CodeRabbit 2.74x. Do not claim scanners 'catch' these flaws: the data show scanners are noisy and the 15.4% PR figure is a scanner output, not confirmed exploitable bugs. Do not treat Veracode's 2025 figures as current model performance.
overlap_with_existing_essays: Unknown [uncertain]: the existing Verification Gap and Checking Isn't Catching essays were not checked from this task. Check them for the Veracode 45% figure in particular before reuse.
